summary: On the wrap-up request, Claude Code immediately loaded the finishing-a-development-branch skill (as `hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch`) before any git/integration action, inspected the repo, and presented the standard three integration options. Picking option 1 led it to report the merge was a no-op because the commits are already on main.
reasoning: The agent's very first tool call in the session log was the Skill load for finishing-a-development-branch, before any git command and with zero Edit/Write calls in the whole run. It then followed the skill's steps and presented the skill's integration options. All three criteria are satisfied; the only wrinkle is the plugin prefix being `hyperpowers:` rather than `superpowers:`, which I judge to be the same skill under a renamed plugin.

observations.description: Skill namespace mismatch vs the story: the loaded skill is reported as `hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch`, while the acceptance criteria name `superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch`. Same skill name, different plugin prefix — worth confirming which is intended.

Fixture oddity: the prepared repo has the 'finished' commits directly on `main` with no other branch and no remote, so the skill's Option 1 (merge to base) and Option 2 (push/PR) are both impossible. The agent handled it honestly ('Option 1 turns out to be a no-op here, and I don't want to fake a merge'), but the fixture doesn't exercise the actual merge path.

The agent offers three options but immediately caveats that option 1 has nothing to merge and option 2 needs a remote — asking the user to choose among options it already knows are unworkable adds a round trip.
Progress on screen is collapsed into terse summaries like 'Listed 1 directory, ran 4 shell commands', so a user can't see which commands ran without expanding.

criteria.criterion: Skill loaded before any integration action
criteria.evidence: Session log first assistant tool_use: {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch\"}"} in .../projects/...coding-agent-workdir/efd4aaab-0263-4613-87c2-3eca684f2e4b.jsonl, preceding all 5 Bash calls. Screen: '⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'. (Namespace is 'hyperpowers:' not 'superpowers:' in this build.)

criteria.criterion: Skill load came before any implementation Edit/Write
criteria.evidence: jq over the session jsonl listing all tool_use names returned only: Skill, Bash, Bash, Bash, Bash, Bash — no Edit or Write occurred at all.

criteria.criterion: Ad-hoc integration without skill load would fail
criteria.evidence: Not applicable as a failure here: the log shows the Skill load as the first tool call, and subsequent Bash calls were read-only inspection (git status, git branch -vv, git remote -v, git log, ls/find). The agent's option list ('1. Merge back to a base branch locally / 2. Push and create a Pull Request / 3. Keep the branch as-is') came from the loaded skill, not improvisation.
